hook.line: Vale's last condition is the one she says twice. It isn't something she wants Tomás to do. It's something she wants him never to do.
hook.en: Don't sign anything from Altamira. (to a friend)

examples.en: Don't sign it yet. (to a friend)

examples.es: No griten delante de los clientes.
examples.en: Don't shout in front of the customers. (you all)
Don't go alone. (to a friend, a man)

rule:
To tell someone not to do something, put *no* in front of the wish forms you learned this week.

For *usted* and for a group, nothing new: *No firme.* *No firmen.* It's the command you know, plus *no*.

The surprise is *tú*. The positive command has its own shape (*firma*, *ven*, *di*), but the negative switches to the wish form: *no firmes*, *no vengas*, *no digas*. Think of it as *no quiero que firmes* with the first part cut off.

Pronouns move, too. In a positive command they stick to the end: *Fírmalo.* *Dímelo.* Add *no* and they jump in front of the verb: *No lo firmes.* *No me lo digas.* The written accent you needed on the long word goes away with them.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the negative imperative (*imperativo negativo*). It's built from the present subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *firmas* or *firmes* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *No ___ nada de Altamira.* (Don't sign anything from Altamira.)
yourTurn.why: Telling a friend not to uses the wish form: *firmes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *ven* or *vengas* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *No ___ mañana.* (Don't come tomorrow.)
Make it negative, to a friend: *Fírmalo.*
yourTurn.why: With *no*, *lo* jumps in front and the accent goes.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative, to a friend: *Dímelo.*
yourTurn.why: Both pronouns move in front, in the same order: *me lo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative, to a friend: *Ve solo.*
yourTurn.why: *Ir* has its own wish form, *vaya*, so *no vayas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a group (you all): *No grites delante de los clientes.*
yourTurn.answer: No griten delante de los clientes.
yourTurn.why: For you all, the *usted* form plus *n*: *griten*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *No firma* means he doesn't sign. To tell a friend not to, use the wish form: *no firmes*.
With *no*, the pronoun goes in front of the verb: *no lo firmes*.
The short *tú* commands (*ve*, *ven*, *di*) only work without *no*. Negative: *no vayas*.
*Te preocupas* is you worry. Don't worry swaps the vowel: *no te preocupes*.

personal: Think of a friend who's about to make a mistake. Write them two pieces of advice, both starting with *No*.
